items.content_text: In an Oct 30 press-conference transcript, China's National Energy Administration says that by Sep 30, 24 provinces had issued supporting measures for green-power direct connection, and localities had approved 12 projects serving computing facilities, more than 10% of all approved direct-connection projects. The agency also projects that national compute electricity use will add more than 100 billion kWh annually during the 2026–2030 plan period and reach 800 billion kWh in 2030, about 6% of national electricity use. These are regulator-reported aggregate counts and agency projections. The transcript provides no project names, capacity, commissioning, metered supply, electricity cost, renewable share, emissions or useful-compute output, and it does not identify which projects are governed by the May 2026 multi-user notice.
items.title: China's energy regulator reports 12 approved green-power direct-connection projects for computing facilities

items.content_text: A preprint re-evaluates the Neural Thickets perturb-select-vote procedure and reports that much of its measured gain does not require perturbing model weights. The authors apply a fixed random bias to output logits, select members using 200 labeled task examples, then vote across selected members. In author-reported tests on language models up to 7B parameters, this approach is statistically indistinguishable from full-weight perturbations on 22 of 28 matched model–task pairs and significantly better on three and worse on three; effects vary by task, and on USPTO the raw accuracy partly reflects a majority-class predictor. On vision tasks with train-test shift, the authors attribute gains primarily to output recalibration. The work offers an alternative explanation for the measured gains, not evidence that nearby weight-space structure is absent or that the method improves general model capability.
tags: École nationale des ponts et chaussées
items.title: Logit perturbations reproduce many reported Neural Thickets gains without changing weights

items.content_text: A distinct Oct 29 arXiv paper by Google and The University of Hong Kong authors, arXiv:2610.40578, introduces a platform-agnostic framework named VeriCUA. An earlier Oct 19 paper from a different author group uses the same acronym for a learned GUI reward verifier; the two papers are separate. The later framework gathers evidence through GUI and code checks, links findings to observed sources, and can abstain when evidence does not settle a requirement. Across five reported benchmark settings, the authors find higher agreement with reference labels than selected verifier baselines. The results are author-reported and limited to the studied environments and model setup; offline unresolved cases may fall back to an initial VLM judgment, and the paper reports substantially higher token and call costs than single-call judging.
items.title: Google and HKU report platform-agnostic verification for computer-use agents

items.content_text: A distinct Oct 19 arXiv paper, 2610.26469, introduces a learned GUI reward verifier also named VeriCUA; its authors and method differ from a later Oct 29 paper using the same acronym (arXiv:2610.40578). The earlier work trains a Judge to select checks and decide when to stop while a frozen Probe inspects live GUI state. The authors report higher agreement than prompted and passive verifiers across OSWorld, MobileWorld and WebArena-Verified, and a bounded downstream Actor-RL gain. Code and configuration details are publicly linked, but no independent reproduction was performed. The reported token comparison counts Probe use, not the full Judge, training or infrastructure cost.
tags: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
items.title: Earlier VeriCUA paper reports learned GUI verification and reward gains

items.content_text: Japan's Economic and Fiscal Policy Council held its fifteenth meeting on 29 October 2026 with AI-driven economic and social change as a formal agenda item. Advisory members submitted proposals on broader public and business AI use, labor-market transition, AI-agent responsibility, AI-related productivity and token-cost measurement, cybersecurity, domestic capability and education. A government paper described ongoing work toward a 2030 vision, cross-government reform principles and possible legal and safety-control updates, with a year-end interim summary planned. These are submitted proposals and stated work directions; the meeting record does not establish adopted law, budget allocations, implementation or measured outcomes.
items.title: Japan's economic-policy council sets out proposals on AI, work and national capability

items.content_text: ShallowDefend is a work-in-progress preprint proposing an Assess → Decide → Respond format: on each turn, a model assesses user intent, commits to a parseable safety decision, and generates a response conditioned on that decision. The authors train the decision with either a self-verified reward based on known harmful or benign dialogue labels, or an external judge reward. Across five multi-turn safety benchmarks, the paper reports average safe rates of 90.4% and 93.4% for the self-reward variant on Llama 3.1 8B and Qwen3 8B, respectively; its external-reward variant scores 92.9% and 87.6%. The paper reports that its safety lead holds under six judges. These are author-reported comparisons on two backbones, not independent replication or evidence of deployment-grade safety.
items.title: ShallowDefend trains an explicit early decision for multi-turn safety defense

items.content_text: The Ramanujan Challenge authors report an AI-assisted workflow for reviewing research-level mathematical submissions in natural language, computer algebra and Lean. It executes submitted Python under a fixed environment, has separate agents summarize the proof and code, compares those summaries, then presents the result to a human reviewer. Against one-shot Claude Opus 5 judgments on the same challenge set, the authors report that false 'Correct' verdicts fell from 23.4% to 5.8% for 137 natural-language proofs and from 38.3% to 3.3% for 120 CAS/Lean artifacts. Agreement with one human evaluator rose from 65.7% to 66.4% for proofs and from 45.8% to 58.3% for code. The paper says each artifact was reviewed by one human without cross-checking; participants self-selected and reported their tools. These are one paper's results, not independent confirmation of generality or reduced expert workload.
items.title: A structured pipeline cut false positive grading of research level mathematical proofs, but generality remains untested

items.content_text: OpenAI announced a recurring Community Safety Report on violence prevention and other community-safety issues, with the first report planned for early 2027 and six-month updates. It also says it is tightening responses to detailed requests about past mass attacks, extending teen limits to practical weapons and security-system information even without signs of violent intent, and developing context-sensitive chat interruption and account pauses for repeated conversations indicating violent fixation. OpenAI says rollout begins in the coming weeks. Earlier OpenAI materials already described a teen experience and age-prediction system with age-appropriate safeguards and an adult correction route. The new announcement describes additional restrictions, but neither the new nor prior material establishes deployment reach, accuracy or real-world safety outcomes.
items.title: OpenAI announces expanded violence safeguards and recurring community-safety reporting

items.content_text: The United States and Finland signed a Technology Prosperity Deal memorandum of understanding on October 29. The document includes intended cooperation on an open and secure super-intelligence stack—which its footnote says Finland uses to mean artificial intelligence—including technology-stack exports, financing coordination, telecommunications and international standards. The MOU is not legally binding and commits neither government to spend funds. The announcement establishes the signed framework and stated intentions, not implementation, financing, deployment or measurable effects.
items.title: United States and Finland sign a nonbinding deal covering cooperation on an open and secure AI stack

items.content_text: An arXiv paper reports that construction cues in several automated-interpretability evaluation pipelines can predict stored scores without reading feature explanations. On rebuilt marks for 500 GPT-2 small features, the authors report a centre-mark rule at 0.979 balanced accuracy versus 0.838 for stored scorers, and a mark-count rule at 0.969. Their separate preregistered ranking test did not show that the tested simulation cue reordered features; an explanation-sensitive scorer exceeded explanation-free baselines on random-offset natural windows. These are bounded author-reported results, not evidence that automated interpretability as a field is invalid.
items.title: A paper reports explanation-free shortcuts in automated interpretability evaluations

items.content_text: A new preprint reports that an activation probe can identify, before generation, the specific model call that discloses a protected string after peer pressure in synthetic multi-agent episodes. On held-out Qwen3-32B episodes, the author reports 0.98 AUROC and catches 31 of 38 leaking calls at a threshold flagging 5% of benign control calls. At that threshold, however, 59% of refusing episodes have at least one alarm. The more attractive threshold catching 10 of 38 leaking episodes (26%) while flagging about 5% of refusing episodes was selected on the test set; a threshold set on training episodes flagged 29% of refusing test episodes. The study uses mocked tools and fake secrets, and a trained text classifier comes close. This is a bounded paper-reported warning signal, not evidence of effective real-world intervention or broad transfer.
items.title: A pre-output activation probe predicts agent disclosure in synthetic peer-pressure episodes

items.content_text: Mistral says it released an improved Mistral Large 4 checkpoint as open weights on Oct 29, following an Oct 6 public preview and three additional weeks of reinforcement learning. The model card lists a 1.05T-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 49B active parameters per token (52B including embeddings and output layers), and the checkpoint is listed on Hugging Face under a modified MIT-style license that requires a separate license for model-as-a-service businesses. Mistral reports updated coding, cybersecurity, finance and browsing results, including 48% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index with 47% fewer tokens per task than its stated comparison, and 51% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index. These are vendor-reported results; the full technical report is not yet available and no independent evaluation or local model run was conducted here.
items.title: Mistral releases improved Mistral Large 4 weights with updated coding and cyber claims

items.content_text: A preprint introduces LRMoE, which selects backward token–expert contributions using a local gradient-impact score, plans expert placement under memory and communication constraints, then compacts retained rows before communication and grouped GEMMs. On eight Hopper GPUs with an 80 GiB per-GPU budget, the authors report 21.2–44.8% lower cumulative MoE-layer time to four matched loss targets than SYMI for Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B, despite additional training steps. These are author-reported results on two configurations and a locally reused Alpaca corpus; they exclude non-MoE layers and are not whole-model end-to-end savings. The appendix proves optimality only for a fixed-count, equal-row-cost additive sum of isolated projection-gradient perturbations. No independent reproduction was performed.
items.title: LRMoE reports faster memory-constrained training for two sparse MoE models

items.content_text: An October 27 arXiv preprint introduces leverage, the Fisher quadratic form of a weight update divided by the same form for a random direction of equal size at the same checkpoint. Across released Olmo-3, Tülu-3, Zephyr and OLMo-2 checkpoints, the author reports leverage near 1 for two pretraining windows on a 51,167-token mixed corpus, about 5 for SFT, hundreds to low thousands for RL-Zero/RLVR, and values from hundreds to tens of thousands for DPO. Controlled training and one released OLMo-2 DPO recipe rerun support some of the reported contrasts. The paper also reports that a sign-structure term predicts damage from random delta sparsification in tested cases. These are author-reported research results. The metric measures local next-token distribution change, not task capability; results are bounded by the corpora and training regimes studied, and no independent reproduction was performed here.
items.title: A preprint defines a Fisher leverage measure for comparing language-model weight updates

items.content_text: A new preprint introduces WxCrop, a workflow that joins dated weather, crop maps, growing calendars and county-level insured-loss records to estimate crop hazard and loss fractions in Florida. The authors report hazard-index discrimination and retrospective loss-model checks, including held-out-year storm losses within 2% in aggregate and county citrus-production ranking correlation of 0.63 across 110 county-seasons. These are author-reported retrospective results; the paper does not establish prospective forecast utility, field-level accuracy or operational benefit.
items.title: WxCrop paper links weather hazards to county-level crop-loss estimates

items.content_text: Fuzhou Municipal SASAC reports that officials were briefed on construction progress and technology applications at the national AI application test base for employment services. A later municipal profile says the city talent group is leading the project and describes a planned compute, employment-data and sector-model stack. At an Oct 22–24 workshop, official and government-hosted reports describe discussion of technical work, standards, evaluation safety and future pilot scenarios. These are reported project activities and plans; the sources do not establish deployed service performance or employment outcomes.
tags: Fuzhou Municipal State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission
items.title: Fuzhou reports progress on an employment-focused AI test base and convenes a technical workshop

items.content_text: An Oct. 29 arXiv preprint presents Soei, a provenance and verification observability design, alongside a prototype study of 45 real VS Code Copilot agent-mode sessions from one developer. The authors report 102,233 records and 20,577 tool executions. Their audited rule-based classifier yields a bias-corrected estimate that 23.4% of code-editing episodes ended without an independent check after the last edit (95% CI 17.1–35.7); 57.8% of edit-backed to-dos marked complete had no recorded proof between the last edit and completion. The authors also report that their content-free, hash-chained ledger occupied about 20% of the raw transcript size and detected a tamper test. The private corpus is not released. These are author-reported single-user pilot findings, not population estimates or evidence that a classified check establishes correctness.
items.title: Soei preprint reports a single-developer audit of coding-agent evidence and history

items.content_text: An Oct. 28 arXiv preprint introduces LLM-PowerTrace, a reported collection of GPU power traces across fine-tuning and serving. The authors describe 1,788 fine-tuning runs and 405 inference runs on NVIDIA L40S, A100, H100 and H200 GPUs, with nominal 100 ms device telemetry, and report fitted mean-power errors in the low single digits on evaluated held-out regimes. They say the complete dataset will be released upon acceptance; the currently described explorer exposes selected reference traces. The preprint does not establish independent reproduction, facility-level energy measurement or grid effects.
items.title: LLM-PowerTrace reports time-resolved GPU power data for AI compute

items.content_text: Canada's federal, provincial and territorial privacy commissioners and ombuds passed a resolution urging responsible AI development, procurement and use in health care and health research, according to an October 29 release from the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada. The release summarizes six principles and calls for legally required governance and accountability frameworks in health AI, updated research-ethics guidance and stronger ethics-board capacity. The full linked resolution could not be retrieved, and the recommendations are not evidence of enacted rules, institutional adoption or measured outcomes.
tags: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
Federal, provincial and territorial privacy regulators
items.title: Canadian privacy regulators call for stronger governance of AI in health care and research

items.content_text: OpenAI's October 29 system-card addendum identifies GPT-6 Luna (October 29) as an updated ChatGPT model, described as more concise and less overly agreeable than the October 7 version. The card assigns the update High capability classifications in cybersecurity and biological/chemical domains and reports 99.91% robustness on its instruction-hierarchy evaluation. OpenAI also reports improvement on four selected under-18 safe-completion evaluations, but mixed or lower comparisons on several HealthBench and MentalHealthBench measures. These are provider-run results; this review did not independently reproduce them or establish safety outcomes in ordinary use.
items.title: OpenAI updates GPT-6 Luna with mixed safety-evaluation results
